transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-21
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Anika Shah (Redwood Partnerships); Lena Novak (Magnetar Head of Partnerships), Omar Aziz (Magnetar CTO), Priya Menon (Cloud Architect), Samir Rao (BD)

Summary (auto):
Quick channel intro + technical discovery for reseller/onboarding scenario. Magnetar is EMEA-focused systems integrator/reseller with managed edge GPU offering; interested in both marketplace and private deployment flows. Primary concerns: integration patterns for VPC/on-prem, certified GPU/instance types, performance guarantees, compliance (SOC2, KMS), and partner economics. Next: pricing and benchmark plan to validate latency and throughput.

Topics (auto):
- Partner model and commerce flows
- Private deployment / VPC networking details
- GPU compatibility and perf targets
- Security/compliance questions (SOC 2, SSO, KMS)
- Pilot/benchmark plan

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: All right everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Maya from Redwood, I think Diego's on for the technical bits. Um quick round robin?
[00:08] Lena: Hi, Lena here at Magnetar, I run Partnerships, excited to talk channel stuff and the tech flow.
[00:12] Omar: Omar, CTO, I'll mostly listen for the infra bits.
[00:15] Priya: Priya, cloud architect, will have a few questions about VPC and network egress.
[00:20] Diego: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: partner/commercial model, integration touchpoints, technical requirements and then next steps. Sound OK?
[00:28] Samir: Yep, that works.
[00:30] Maya: I'll start with a very brief overview of Redwood and our partner programs cause I know Magnetar has both reseller and managed service wings. We offer hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity and private deployments for customers who want VPC or on-prem. For partners we have reseller SKUs and a private deployment enablement flow.
[00:50] Lena: Quick Q—how opinionated is the partner pricing? Like do you allow flexible margins and marketplace listings? We have channel partners who expect co-terminate billing.
[00:58] Maya: Yes, we have a partner pricing matrix. There is a marketplace listing option and a reseller discount for committed monthly minimums. There is some flexibility—volume tiers, co-terming, and white-labeling conversation can be had, but legal needs to sign an addendum. I can send the matrix after this call.
[01:15] Lena: Great.
[01:18] Diego: From the tech side, Magnetar asked earlier about private deployments—there are two patterns we see: a VPC-hosted private control plane with customer-managed compute in their VPC (or partner-managed in their account), or a fully on-prem package. The VPC path is fastest; on-prem is a packaged appliance and typically includes additional support SLA.
[01:40] Priya: For VPC, is it connector-based? Do we need to open specific ports? We prefer zero inbound rules to our infra if possible.
[01:48] Diego: Good question—our VPC flow uses outbound-only peering (we call it egress-only tunnels) for the control plane, and there's an optional private peering for higher throughput. Mostly you configure SGs to allow outbound to Redwood endpoints and we negotiate a peering or VPN. It's not like you have to expose services publicly.
[02:05] Omar: And what about the KV cache / prefix caching? If we run a managed pool for customers at edge sites, how does the KV cache behave across clusters? Does it centralize or stay local?
[02:15] Diego: The runtime supports local KV cache per serving cluster. We do optional cross-cluster cache invalidation but by default caches are local to the instance to keep latency predictable. For Magnetar's use-case—edge pools—we'd recommend local KV cache with a warm-up strategy; we can add a short-lived cross-sync for hot keys.
[02:40] Priya: That sounds promising. Another concern—GPU types. Our edge nodes vary; we have A100s in core datacenters and L4s at many edge colo sites. Any limitations?
[02:52] Diego: We certify a set of instance types; the main ones are NVIDIA A100, H100 for heavy throughput, and L4 for lower-cost inference on smaller models. There's also H900-class in some clouds; the runtime has kernel selection heuristics so it will pick optimized kernels for each hardware. The tricky part is quantization and memory layout differences across GPUs—we've got quant profiles per GPU class.
[03:15] Omar: OK, and does Redwood provide pre-built container images for on-prem or partner-managed clusters?
[03:20] Diego: Yes, we ship container images and Helm charts for private deployments. For the on-prem appliance we also provide an OVA for air-gapped installs. You get versioned images and an operator for upgrades.
[03:30] Lena: A bit about compliance—our clients in finance ask for SOC 2 type II and key management with customer-controlled KMS. What's supported?
[03:40] Maya: We are SOC 2 certified (we can send the attestation), and for private deployments we integrate with customer KMS or HSM via standard APIs. For hosted API we offer envelope encryption and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) options via KMS integrations in select tiers.
[03:58] Priya: Does that include audit logs at token/request level? Our legal team often needs per-request traceability for data lineage.
[04:05] Diego: We provide detailed audit logging, including request IDs, model versions, and token-level metrics in the console for Dedicated and Private. Some fields are redacted by default in hosted but there are enterprise packages for extended retention.
[04:20] Samir: From a GTM lens—do you allow co-selling? Will Redwood join regional customer calls?
[04:25] Maya: Absolutely—co-sell is part of our partner program for strategic deals. We can provide an AE/SE assist for named accounts, and we have MDF for top-tier partners.
[04:36] Lena: Pricing—do you do committed reserved capacity for partners or only end customers?
[04:40] Maya: We do reserved capacity contracts for both; partners can buy capacity and resell or we can do pass-through dedicated pools per customer. There's flexibility based on expected throughput and commitment length.
[04:52] Priya: A couple of nitty-gritty: what is the typical cold-start latency, and do you support continuous batching? We care about tail latency for chat apps.
[05:05] Diego: Cold-start time depends on model size and GPU type. For LLM sizes under 20B on A100 w/ optimized kernels, warm-generation latency can be sub-50ms per token in continuous streaming mode, but cold-start can be seconds if KV cache/weights not resident. We support continuous batching to improve throughput while aiming for latency SLOs; the routing policy can prioritize low-latency pools.
[05:33] Omar: Those 50ms numbers are optimistic—what SLA do you commit to?
[05:38] Maya: For Dedicated we publish latency SLOs in the contract tied to model classes and sequence lengths. For Hosted we provide benchmarks and we can commit to custom SLAs for enterprise Reseller contracts.
[05:50] Priya: On network egress—if we host in EMEA, can we guarantee data residency and region locking?
[05:58] Diego: Yes, region pinning is supported. Private deployments obviously give you full control. For hosted we have region-specific endpoints; customers can restrict routing to EMEA clusters.
[06:10] Lena: Questions on marketplace—if we list Redwood in our marketplace with a markup, does Redwood handle billing or do we?
[06:17] Maya: We have both handled-billing marketplace flows and partner-billing (reseller). Handled-billing is simpler for customers; reseller billing allows you to control invoicing and margins.
[06:28] Samir: Any prebuilt integrations for partner-managed customer onboarding? Like we need automation for tenant creation and RBAC linking to our SAML/SSO.
[06:36] Diego: We expose APIs for programmatic tenant provisioning, RBAC, and SSO (SAML/OIDC). For partner-managed onboarding we can provide templates and a webhook/event flow for provisioning.
[06:48] Priya: On RBAC—can roles be mapped to our internal groups automatically?
[06:52] Diego: Yes, via SAML attribute mapping you can map groups to roles and we support SCIM for user sync.
[06:58] Lena: Switching gear—tech deep dive. If we want to run a pilot on a customer at scale, what's the minimum cluster spec you'd recommend?
[07:06] Diego: Depends on model and qps. For a chat-like workload with a 13B model, we'd recommend at least two A100s for HA if low-latency is key. For batch-heavy workloads, more smaller GPUs with batching is more cost-effective. We'll prepare a sizing sheet.
[07:24] Omar: For the edge—we might prefer L4s for inference to keep costs down. How do model quantization options affect quality?
[07:31] Diego: We have quant profiles 8-bit and 4-bit tuned per model family. 4-bit can introduce some quality delta; we provide eval harnesses to measure regen/accuracy metrics. Redwood Optimize recommends which quantization to use per workload.
[07:50] Priya: Can you run our eval set for a quick quality check? We have a canonical prompt set for a banking customer.
[07:56] Diego: Yes, we can run it. We'll need the eval prompts and expected metrics. I'll run on L4 and A100 to show delta.
[08:03] Maya: Diego, can you note that as an action item?
[08:06] Diego: Yep. I'll prepare a plan with sample prompts, metrics to capture, and an estimated runtime.
[08:12] Samir: Legal and procurement—timeline expectations? We often have an RFP/PO process.
[08:17] Maya: For partners we usually have an MSA and reseller addendum. Typical legal review is 2-4 weeks. If there's an RFP, we can provide a security and compliance pack.
[08:28] Lena: Another thing—are there restrictions on embedding models or rehosting model weights? Some of our customers want to keep models on-prem.
[08:36] Diego: For private deployment we can host customer-owned models. For hosted we serve via our catalog; we do not allow rehosted model weights on the hosted shared infrastructure. On-prem/private gives you full control over weights and models.
[08:52] Omar: Ok good. On monitoring—do you expose per-tenant token-level cost estimates in real time? Customers want chargebacks.
[08:59] Diego: Yes, in Redwood Console we include token-level cost breakdowns, per-route breakdowns, and exportable reports for chargeback. For partner-managed customers, we can export via API to your billing system.
[09:13] Priya: We need to validate network egress costs—do you have suggestions for minimizing cross-region traffic for inference?
[09:20] Diego: Best practice is region pinning and local caches; run inference close to data and use prefix/KV caching to avoid repeated streaming across regions. Also batching reduces per-token overhead.
[09:33] Maya: I want to surface a few customer stories—we've worked with a fintech VAR that used private deployment with BYOK and A100s for low-latency trading alerts. They were able to reduce per-token cost by 32% after tuning batching and quantization.
[09:48] Lena: Are any partner references in EMEA you can share?
[09:51] Maya: I can share anonymized references; let me check which partners are public.
[09:55] Priya: Quick probe—what's the rollback story if a model rollout degrades quality?
[10:01] Diego: We support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to earlier model variants. Redflags trigger alerts in the console and can auto-roll back if quality metrics cross thresholds.
[10:12] Omar: Is automatic fallback per-tenant or global?
[10:16] Diego: Per-route and per-tenant rules are supported.
[10:20] Samir: A commercial point—what are standard margins for resellers?
[10:24] Maya: They vary by tier; typical is 10-25% depending on commitment and co-selling. Top tier partners with MDF get better. We'll include banding in the pricing doc.
[10:35] Lena: Do you support white-labeling the console for MSPs?
[10:39] Maya: There's a limited white-label path for strategic partners. It requires additional terms for support and branding.
[10:45] Priya: Another technical question—does the runtime have GPU affinity policies so we can dedicate certain GPU classes to certain customers? We need to isolate high value customers onto H100s.
[10:54] Diego: Yes, the scheduler supports GPU class affinity and allocation pools so you can pin customers to capacity tiers and ensure isolation.
[11:05] Priya: In that case, does sharing a pool risk noisy neighbor?
[11:09] Diego: We mitigate noisy neighbor with isolation primitives and cgroup-level resource limits, and we recommend dedicated pools for top-tier clients.
[11:20] Maya: I'm going to ping our partner playbook link into the chat—it's the short overview of co-sell, technical enablement, and onboarding.
[11:27] [file shared: /redwood/partner-playbook.pdf]
[11:30] Lena: Any limitations on model size for the on-prem OVA? We've seen appliances struggle with >70B weights.
[11:37] Diego: OVA is fine but you'll need sufficient NVMe and GPU memory; very large models >70B often need model parallelism which we can support but it's more complex. We'll scope that in the sizing doc.
[11:52] Omar: For the benchmark plan—can you include a latency P95 target and a cost per 1M tokens estimate for each GPU class?
[11:58] Diego: Yes, that's in scope for the benchmark plan. We'll include P50/P95/P99, throughput, and cost per million tokens for A100/H100/L4 with batching knobs.
[12:10] Priya: Will the benchmark plan run in our environment or Redwood's? We prefer to see numbers on our infra.
[12:15] Diego: Ideally in your infra or in a mirrored environment. For speed we can run a quick Delta test on Redwood Dedicated and then reproduce on Magnetar test cluster.
[12:26] Samir: Legal—what's the turnaround for an NDA?
[12:29] Maya: We can do a standard partner NDA in 3-5 business days.
[12:33] Lena: Good. I'm also thinking of go-to-market: we can co-host a webinar in EMEA to introduce Redwood to our MSP customers.
[12:42] Maya: We'd love that. We can provide a joint deck and SE to present demos.
[12:48] [short silence / ambient typing]
[13:00] Diego: A quick technical aside—if Magnetar plans to run multiple small clusters at edge sites, we'll want to discuss image distribution and updates. We have an update operator that can roll images with canary and health checks.
[13:18] Priya: Can we integrate with our terraform modules for provisioning?
[13:22] Diego: Yes, we have modules and examples; we can share a terraform provider snippet.
[13:27] Priya: Great.
[13:30] Maya: I see we're at about 35 minutes—maybe wrap up with concrete next steps.
[13:35] Lena: From Magnetar side: we'll send cluster sizing and compliance checklist, and confirm legal contact.
[13:41] Maya: From Redwood: I'll send partner pricing and partner playbook; Diego will send the benchmark plan and a template for eval prompts.
[13:50] Diego: One more thing—for the pilot, we'll need a short sync with your infra team to exchange network/IP ranges and a preflight checklist.
[13:58] Priya: I'll schedule the infra sync.
[14:02] Maya: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
[14:07] Lena: Thanks all.
[14:09] Maya: Bye.
